pairs.why: Both put the coffin on grass with trees and bushes, but B has a quieter backdrop and keeps the single hero central; A adds an open lid and purple lining, which is a story detail the real cards don't have.
Both use the same quiet tone-on-tone wavy purple backdrop with no props, so staging gives no reason to choose.
A has quiet, evenly banded concentric rings like the real cards, while B has a bright hot-spot glow behind the hat that competes with it.
A floats on the wavy field with no ground shadow, as the real cards do, while B adds a contact shadow under the coil, which makes it sit on a surface.
A's door fills the frame with ivy hugging both edges, close to the real card, while B shows a smaller door with more wall around it and a stone step.
A's chair stands on a flat ledge against a gradient backdrop like the real card, while B uses a steep angular slab with a hard corner.
A's wood floor and striped wall match the real cards' simple staging and the hero is larger; B has more empty floor, but both are quiet.
B has a large central hero with a few big shapes (one tree, path, bushes); A shrinks the table and scatters more bushes, trees and flowers.
